articles.title: Docker Mailserver has 22 title matches because mail services do not advertise a dashboard name
articles.excerpt: Docker Mailserver has 22 title matches because mail services do not advertise a dashboard name Docker Mailserver is a containerized mail server, not a web application with one branded login page. A Zo…
articles.body: Docker Mailserver has 22 title matches because mail services do not advertise a dashboard name Docker Mailserver is a containerized mail server, not a web application with one branded login page. A ZoomEye title query for the project name will miss most deployments because the mail ports produce SMTP, IMAP, POP3, or TLS banners rather than the software name. The low title count is a signature limitation, not a measure of the mail footprint. On 2026-11-17, title="Docker Mailserver" returned 22 total matches at 07:47:09 +08:00. http.body="Docker Mailserver" returned 528 at 07:47:11 +08:00. Both used sub_type=all , page 1, and pagesize=1 . The body matches may include documentation, repositories, and project pages, so neither number should be treated as a server population.
articles.author: andreagomez

articles.title: Hot experts, cold RAM: running a big MoE on a machine with more memory than VRAM
articles.excerpt: Two budgets, and only one of them is expensive Every local deployment spends against two budgets at once: the size of That is what Strata is for. It is forked from llama.cpp and built for llama.cpp is…
articles.body: Two budgets, and only one of them is expensive Every local deployment spends against two budgets at once: the size of the model and the price of the memory holding it. VRAM is the one people reach for first, and it is the one that costs the most per gigabyte. System DDR is fast, vast and cheap; GPU memory is fast, small and expensive. An inference engine that can put weights in the second place changes the bill. That is what Strata is for. It is forked from llama.cpp and built for memory efficiency: it keeps resident only the experts that are hot – the ones actually in use – and leaves the rest parked. That is how big MoE models run on small RAM.

articles.title: Logs Aren't an Audit Trail: Debugging Business Data in Spring Boot
articles.excerpt: A production support ticket comes in: "Why was this account deactivated?" You check the database: id = 1042 status = DEACTIVATED Then you search the application logs: 2026-10-12T09:42:18Z INFO Account…
articles.body: A production support ticket comes in: "Why was this account deactivated?" You check the database: id = 1042 status = DEACTIVATED Then you search the application logs: 2026-10-12T09:42:18Z INFO AccountService Account 1042 updated successfully The application processed an update. But that doesn't answer the question. What was the previous status? Who initiated the change? Did the transaction actually commit? Was this the first transition, or had the account changed several times? This is a distinction that becomes important when supporting production applications: Application logs describe execution. Audit trails describe changes to business data. They are related, but they aren't interchangeable. 1.

articles.excerpt: Expo Exact is an app framework written in Rust, without React, that Charlie Cheever, co-founder of Expo, previewed as a pre-alpha on November 9, 2026. Its interface is written in a new language called…
articles.body: Expo Exact is an app framework written in Rust, without React, that Charlie Cheever, co-founder of Expo, previewed as a pre-alpha on November 9, 2026. Its interface is written in a new language called Contract, and Cheever describes it as "agent native": designed so that an AI agent can build, run, see and test the app. When Expo's co-founder ships a React-free framework, those of us who maintain React Native apps are left with one question: is React Native dead? I read the announcement and the repository's README. I did not build an app with Exact; what follows is a reading of what Expo published, from someone who ships React Native and Expo apps for clients, writes native Swift and builds agents.

articles.body: 依實際工作需求選擇小型模型 先選擇支援你所需輸入類型的模型。可以試用 Qwen3 4B 作為小型文字基準模型；如果也需要圖片輸入，可以試用 Gemma 3 4B ；若要測試數學或結構化任務，可以把 Phi-4-mini 當作第二個文字基準模型。這些都是適合在自己的電腦上測試的候選模型。它們的相對品質取決於你的提示詞、語言和驗收標準。 估算可用記憶體 40 億個參數，每個精確使用 4 位元，光儲存原始權重就需要約 2 GB。檔案可能更大，而載入後的模型還需要空間供執行時緩衝區及鍵值快取使用。請為作業系統和推論期間同時執行的其他工作保留記憶體。即使下載的權重不變，更長的上下文仍需要更多記憶體。 Ollama 上下文長度文件 為了讓比較可以重現，先用相同提示詞搭配較短的上下文測試，例如 2,048 個 token，接著再使用工作實際需要的上下文長度。除了延遲，也要記錄是否使用交換空間或將部分運算轉移至 CPU。模型在第一種設定下能放進記憶體，並不表示在第二種設定下也能放得下。 使用 Ollama 進行初次比較 ollama run qwen3:4b ollama run gemma3:4b ollama run phi4-mini ollama ps 一次執行一個模型指令，開始下一個之前先退出前一個聊天。模型載入時，使用 ollama ps 查看分配的上下文及 CPU／GPU 分配比例。比較記憶體和執行時間時，請保持上下文與提示詞設定相同。圖片輸入則應另行針對實際支援圖片的模型測試。 保留通過測試的最小模型 準備一小組固定的代表性提示詞與預期結果。例如，摘要一段短文並保留指定事實，或產生能通過你所使用 schema 驗證的 JSON。在同一台電腦上測量首個 token 的等待時間及輸出速度。記錄失敗的輸出與記憶體使用峰值，不要讓平均值掩蓋它們。保存精確的模型標籤、可取得時的量化設…

articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 16, 1974: The giant Arecibo Observatory in Puerto Rico broadcasts humanity's 1st interstellar message
articles.excerpt: On this day in space! Nov. 16, 1974: The giant Arecibo Observatory in Puerto Rico broadcasts humanity's 1st interstellar message
articles.body: On Nov. 16, 1974, humans sent their first message to the stars in an attempt to contact extraterrestrials. They did this using what was then the largest radio telescope in the world, located at the Arecibo Observatory in Puerto Rico. A group of scientists led by Frank Drake and Carl Sagan sent their message to the M13 star cluster . The message was written in binary code and contained information about human DNA. It also included figures of a human, the solar system and the Arecibo telescope. The idea was that if any aliens were to receive the signal and figure out how to decode it, they would know where it came from. Because M13 is 25,000 light-years away, it will take 25,000 years for any M13 aliens to hear our message — if they are even out there.

articles.title: Relive Starship’s historic Flight 15 with our best photos from launch and ‘Mechazilla’ tower catch
articles.excerpt: See the most epic photos from SpaceX's Starship Flight 15 test flight and historic launch tower catch.
articles.body: STARBASE, Texas — SpaceX has officially wrapped up the 15th test flight of its massive Starship rocket, successfully catching the vehicle's upper stage for the first time. Flight 15 lifted off from SpaceX's Starbase facility here in South Texas on Friday (Nov. 13). The mission was billed as the first to bring both of Starship's stages, the Super Heavy booster and Ship upper stage, back to the launch site for recovery. And, while SpaceX was forced to divert Super Heavy's return to an off-shore splashdown (and explosion), the upper stage managed to survive its 22-hour jaunt in orbit and plunge through the atmosphere for a picture-perfect catch by the launch tower back at Starbase.

articles.excerpt: Nvidia is reportedly not entertaining the idea of bringing Jensen Huang back as CEO following rumors that his allies had established a "war room" to push for his reinstatement.
articles.body: Nvidia is reportedly not entertaining the idea of bringing Jensen Huang back as CEO following rumors that his allies had established a "war room" to push for his reinstatement. The latest turn in the tech giant's whirlwind week arrived yesterday, when the Financial Times reported that the company's ex-boss had supported efforts from his friends in Silicon Valley to see him brought back into the fold . One source said these allies had assembled a "war room" to lay the foundation for his return, but it now seems those efforts may have been for naught. The Nvidia board of directors is not considering reinstating Huang as CEO after he resigned from his position Thursday, November 12, one source told CNBC .

articles.title: Elon Musk says SpaceX’s Starship, already the largest rocket on Earth, will get even bigger with next-gen V4 model
articles.excerpt: Just a day after SpaceX caught the upper stage of its Starship megarocket back at the launch pad for the first time ever, Elon Musk told us that the spacecraft will get even bigger.
articles.body: As usual, SpaceX and its founder Elon Musk are thinking big. The company recovered the upper stage of its Starship megarocket for the first time ever on Saturday (Nov. 14), plucking it out of the sky with the "chopstick" arms of its Texas launch tower. It was a huge moment for SpaceX , bringing its vision of full and rapid rocket reuse much closer to reality. But Elon Musk isn't one to dwell on the past or rest on laurels, so he soon outlined an even more ambitious future for Starship. "Starship V4 will be ~70m [230 feet] long, which is roughly a 40% length increase and allows >60% more propellant load," Musk said via X, the social media platform he owns, on Sunday evening (Nov. 15).
